name: SYS_DEGRADE
title: Structural Erasure
description:
A live camera feed is transformed into a field of ASCII characters and structural marks.

Rather than reproducing the image faithfully, the system extracts edges, contrast relationships, and directional information. The resulting image exists somewhere between language, drawing, and machine vision.

The viewer encounters a version of themselves that is no longer photographic but still recognizable.

This work investigates the threshold at which representation becomes abstraction.

**Artistic Context**

The project is situated within ongoing investigations into memory, archives, digital materiality, and computational culture.

Rather than treating technology as a tool for producing ever more realistic images, What Remains uses reduction, degradation, and abstraction to reveal the structures through which contemporary vision is mediated.

The work proposes that loss is not the opposite of information. Loss can also be a method of understanding.

**Technical Notes**

• Live webcam input
• Real-time ASCII rendering
• Edge-detection and image analysis
• p5.js and HTML5 Canvas
• Browser-based installation environment
• Projection, monitor, or screen-based presentation

name: EFFECT_ROULETTE
title: Image Decomposition Engine
description:
A continuous image decomposition engine.

The system cycles through multiple modes of visual reduction, including bitmap dithering, halftone rendering, chromatic displacement, and signal corruption.

Each transformation reveals a different historical method of image reproduction while exposing the material structure hidden beneath contemporary high-resolution media.

The image oscillates between clarity and collapse.

**Artistic Context**

The project is situated within ongoing investigations into memory, archives, digital materiality, and computational culture.

Rather than treating technology as a tool for producing ever more realistic images, What Remains uses reduction, degradation, and abstraction to reveal the structures through which contemporary vision is mediated.

**Technical Notes**

• Bitmap and halftone processing
• Image decomposition and signal corruption
• HTML5 Canvas API
• Browser-based installation environment
• Projection, monitor, or screen-based presentation

name: CELLULAR_DITHER
title: Emergent Grid Automata
description:
A generative system in which images become living computational ecologies.

Drawing from cellular automata, the work translates visual information into evolving fields of autonomous cells. Patterns emerge, replicate, disappear, and reorganize themselves according to simple local rules.

The resulting image is never fixed. It behaves less like a photograph and more like an organism.

The work explores the possibility that contemporary images are no longer static representations but dynamic systems.

**Artistic Context**

The project is situated within ongoing investigations into memory, archives, digital materiality, and computational culture.

Rather than treating technology as a tool for producing ever more realistic images, What Remains uses reduction, degradation, and abstraction to reveal the structures through which contemporary vision is mediated.

The work proposes that loss is not the opposite of information. Loss can also be a method of understanding.

**Technical Notes**

• Cellular automata simulation
• Emergent generative algorithms
• HTML5 Canvas API
• Browser-based installation environment
• Projection, monitor, or screen-based presentation
